To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human–insect interactions in the context of leisure are complex and multi-layered and that the concept of species-ism is a useful lens for exploring the nuances of such interactions.
human–insect interactions can be viewed as a continuum of experiences that are influenced by our senses of smell and sight, our socio-cultural values and our need for comfort and safety.
human–insect interactions are often influenced by the senses, spatial cues and socio-cultural forces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we understand, experience and interact with the world around us.
how leisure and play are shaped by the social construction of nature, and vice versa.
how we perceive and interact with insects and the implications this has for leisure and the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human–insect interactions in leisure are a complex and dynamic process.
the study of leisure and human–insect interactions has the potential to provide new insights into the human condition, the nature of leisure and the nature of leisure studies.
leisure studies should be at the forefront of this new field of animal–human studies, and that leisure scholars should be at the vanguard of this movement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the leisure industry should be a leader in the promotion of a more pluralistic approach to human–insect relationships and should be at the forefront of the movement to promote a more inclusive, pluralistic approach to leisure and nature.
leisure is not just for humans and the leisure experience can be enhanced when we consider the interplay of human and non-human species in leisure.
leisure can be an important site for the development of a more inclusive, respectful, and ethical human–insect relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should be more open to the possibility that insects can be more than a nuisance, a threat or an object of study.

we should be mindful of the ways in which our leisure experiences are influenced by the social, cultural and historical contexts in which we live, and that our leisure experiences are shaped by the complex interplay of our senses, emotions, and social and cultural norms.
leisure is not only a place for the study of human–insects interactions, it is also an important site for the study of the human–insect relationship.
